**Finding: compliant** — no redline needed.

The agreement already sits at our preferred position on minimum commitments:

- **§ 2.1 (p0013)** — "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," with pay-only-for-ordered-Services language and an express statement that declining a further Order Form is "not a breach or shortfall."
- **§ 7.1 (p0026)** — Vendor may not impose any platform, support, administration or **minimum-use** charge not identified in the Order Form.
- **§ 12.3 (p0051)** — Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or **minimum-volume** commitment.
- **§ 9.4 (p0041)** — Customer has a without-cause termination right with refund of prepaid Fees, so any future Order Form commitment would still have an exit.

I checked the planner's candidate sections (7, 4, 8) and found no take-or-pay, committed spend, shortfall penalty, or volume cap on Customer usage. The only "shortfall" references (§ 22.2–22.3) run in our favour — they concern Vendor underpayment/usage audit true-ups, not a Customer purchase commitment, and so are outside this rule.
